── SonicWall ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
No entry existed for "sonicwall" - fell through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE
(disk_bus="virtio"), while backend/shared/image_profiles.py (the separate table
that governs the ON-DISK file the image importer writes, e.g. sataa.qcow2 vs
virtioa.qcow2) already has "sonicwall": ("sata", ...) - the same two-tables-
drifted class of bug already found for "barracuda" above. QEMU was being launched
with `disk_bus=virtio` attaching a file that was actually written as sataa.qcow2 -
a guaranteed no-bootable-disk mismatch regardless of which table is "right".

reasons.vendor: NPX-1245 (rule #59): RAM 6144 / 4 vCPU = EVE sonicwall.yml; booted through the platform on VM .83 (argv -m 6144 -smp 4, VNC console answers).
reasons.nic:
NIC e1000 -> virtio-net-pci (NPX-824, 2026-09-05). Evidence, not a guess: EVE-NG
PRO v7's own production template for this exact image says `qemu_nic:
virtio-net-pci` (docs/reference/eveng-implementation/raw/templates/sonicwall.yml), so a
shipping product has run this guest on virtio for years - the driver is in the
image. e1000 is emulated packet-by-packet in userspace and can never use the
kernel fast path; virtio can (vhost-net, NPX-823). Live-booted on netplex before
this landed - run recorded in docs/status/PLATFORM-AUDIT.md NPX-824.
reasons.console:
console corrected 2026-07-23 from a live cross-reference against EVE-NG PRO v7's own
production template for this exact image (root@<eveng-box>:/opt/unetlab/html/
templates/intel/sonicwall.yml): `qemu_options: -machine type=pc,accel=kvm
-nographic -rtc base=utc -cpu host` reports console: vnc in the SAME template
despite -nographic - the same "no serial output despite serial being requested"
signal that root-caused cumulus-vx (NPX-297). NOT live-boot-verified here (unlike
cumulus-vx's real `virsh screenshot` proof) - applied from cross-reference evidence
alone, disclosed per rule #31.
